title: Add unit tests for the Editor's checks
body:
The Editor (`app/src/editor.js`) is the most important safety code in the company, and it has no tests yet.

**Do:**
- Add `app/test/editor.test.js` using Node's built-in `node:test` and `node:assert` (no new dependencies).
- Cover `maxWordsFor()` at ages 2, 4, 6 and 8, and `checkStory()` for: a clean story that passes; too few pages; a page over the word limit; the hero's name on too few pages; a banned word; a trademarked name; a web address.
- Add `"test": "node --test test/"` to `app/package.json` and a `npm test` step to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

**Done when:** `cd app && npm test` passes locally and in CI, with no network or keys needed.

title: Offline ledger verifier script
body:
Anyone can download the public ledger at `/api/ledger.json`, but re-checking the hash chain today means trusting `/api/verify` on the same server.

**Do:**
- Add `app/scripts/verify-ledger.mjs` that takes a base URL (default `http://localhost:3100`), fetches `/api/ledger.json`, and recomputes every hash the same way `ledger()` and `verifyChain()` do in `app/src/db.js` (sha256 of canonical sorted-key JSON of `kind`, `actor`, `detail`, `order_id`, `prev_hash`, starting from `GENESIS`).
- Print the number of lines checked and the first broken `seq`, if any; exit non-zero on a break.
- Mention it in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` under the ledger section.

**Done when:** it reports OK against a local run, and reports a break if you edit one line of a saved copy of the JSON.

title: One-command local Postgres with docker compose
body:
The quickstart asks people to paste a `docker run` command for Postgres. A compose file would make it one short command and keep the settings in one place.

**Do:**
- Add `docker-compose.yml` at the repo root with a `postgres:16` service named `db`, port 5432, database `nightlight`, and a named volume so data survives restarts.
- Update `docs/QUICKSTART.md` and the README's "Run it yourself" block to use `docker compose up -d db`, keeping the `docker run` line as an alternative.
- Make sure the `DATABASE_URL` example in `app/.env.example` matches.

**Done when:** a fresh clone can follow the quickstart with `docker compose up -d db` and `./dev.sh` boots and runs migrations.

title: Reading-grade check for Spanish books
body:
The Editor only computes a reading grade for English (`language === "en"` in `app/src/editor.js`). Spanish is one of the 16 languages families can choose.

**Do:**
- Add a Spanish readability score (for example Fernández-Huerta) with a small Spanish syllable counter, used when `language === "es"`.
- Record it in the same `reading_grade` field so it shows up in the `edit_check` ledger line. Do not make it fail a book yet; just record it.
- Add a test with a short Spanish passage.

**Done when:** a Spanish book's `edit_check` line has a non-null `reading_grade`, and English behaviour is unchanged.

title: Make the /tell microphone and live transcript accessible
body:
`/tell` is the page children use most, often with a grown-up helping. It should work well with a keyboard and a screen reader.

**Do (in `app/src/views/tell.js` and `app/public/js/tell.js`):**
- Give the microphone button an accessible name that changes with its state ("Start telling" / "Stop") and `aria-pressed`.
- Put the live transcript in a polite `aria-live` region.
- Make sure every control can be reached and used with Tab, Enter and Space, with a visible focus ring.
- Announce errors (for example the grown-up permission message) with `role="alert"`.

**Done when:** you can tell a story and make a book using only the keyboard, and VoiceOver or NVDA reads the state changes. Include a short note of how you tested it in the PR.

title: Show the Editor's report on the making-of page
body:
Every draft gets an `edit_check` ledger line with `pass`, `issues`, `words`, `reading_grade` and `round`. The making-of page (`app/public/js/order.js`) shows a one-line summary, and it is worth showing exactly what the Editor caught.

**Do:**
- In the making-of timeline, render `edit_check` lines with a small expandable panel: pass or sent back, the list of issues, total words, reading grade, and which round it was.
- Keep the wording warm and short (for example "Sent back once: page 4 had 52 words, the limit is 35").
- No server changes needed: the data is already in `/api/order/:id`.

**Done when:** a book whose first draft failed shows both rounds clearly on `/order/<id>`, and the page still looks right on a phone.
